name: Qin terracotta warriors
summary: Life-size grey terracotta soldiers, horses and officials that the workshops of the First Emperor made for his tomb. Each body is built from standard parts, and the head is finished by hand.

philosophy.core_thesis: An emperor takes an army of clay into the grave, and a factory system of standard parts and hand finish makes each soldier a different man.
design_principles: Make each figure life-size: 175 to 190 cm for a soldier and up to 200 cm for a general.
Build the legs as solid columns and the torso as a hollow coil-built tube, then join the parts with slip.
Press the head in a two-piece mould and add ears, nose, hair and beard by hand to the leather-hard clay.
Give each face its own mouth, brow and moustache, so that no two heads match.
Put the rank in the dress: a general wears armour with a tied bow and a high cap, and an archer kneels.
Fire the grey body in reduction at 950 to 1050 °C, and leave it unglazed.
Paint the fired figure with lacquer and mineral pigments, in red, green, purple and blue.
Stamp or incise the name of the workshop and the master on the body, as a record of who made it.
anti_patterns: A glossy lead glaze over the whole figure
One mould face that repeats on every soldier
A small tabletop figure at half size or less
A white porcelain body with fine enamel painting
Soft rounded armour with no plates or ties
A bright metallic gold finish on the figure

form.shape: Standing and kneeling soldiers, archers, charioteers, generals and officials, at life size, with horses of 150 cm at the shoulder.
form.profile: An upright figure with a straight spine and a slightly turned head; the torso is a long tube and the legs are solid columns.
form.foot_and_rim: A rectangular plinth 3 to 5 cm thick that carries the feet; hands are cast apart and fitted at the wrist, and a hand holds a real bronze weapon.
form.proportion: Soldier height 175 to 190 cm and weight about 110 to 135 kg; the wall of the torso is 2 to 4 cm thick, and the legs are solid.
rules: Keep the full life-size scale for every human figure.
Join the head, arms, torso and legs from separate parts.
Show armour as rows of plates with rivets and ties.
Give the face a calm, direct look with a strong jaw.
Mount each figure on a flat plinth and fit it in a rank.

bodies.rule: Use a local loess clay mixed with fine sand, which fires to a dense grey body. Keep the surface matt and free of any glaze.

methods: coil building of the hollow torso
moulding of heads in two-piece clay moulds
hand modelling of hair, ears and beard
hand carving of armour detail on the leather-hard clay
fitting of cast hands and arms with slip
forming.joins: The parts are joined with wet clay slip at the wrist, neck, waist and ankle. The figure dries slowly for weeks before it goes into the kiln.
forming.details: A stamped workshop name on the body, thumb marks inside the hollow torso, and a small hole in the torso that lets steam out in the kiln.

glaze.pattern: A lacquer base coat and mineral pigments on the dress and the skin. Red, green, purple, blue and white mark the rank and the unit.
glaze.gloss: Matt, below 5 GU; the lacquer layer is dull and the grey clay shows where the paint is lost.
glaze.wear: The paint flakes off in the air within weeks of the dig. The grey clay and the tool marks show, and the pieces are often found broken and mended.

palette.strategy: A grey clay ground with flat mineral colour on the dress: red for coats, green and purple for trousers, flesh pink for faces.

firing.kiln: A brick updraught kiln that holds a few figures at a time, and fires them in a smoky, reducing flame.
processes: drying of the figure for several weeks
firing in reduction to a grey body
lacquer base coat on the fired figure
firing.scale: About 8000 soldiers, 130 chariots and 670 horses in four pits, made by a state workshop system in some 40 years.
firing.signs: Grey colour from reduction, stamped workshop marks, mould seams hidden by hand work, and joins at the wrist and waist.

pieces.form: Standing infantryman with a tunic, a topknot and open hands that held a spear
Kneeling archer in armour, right knee down, hair in a knot
General in plate armour with a bow at the chest and a tall cap
Chariot horse with a short mane, cut ears and open nostrils
Civil official with long robes and folded hands, about life size

positive: unglazed fired clay with matt surface
individual face with moustache and topknot
plate armour with rivets and ties
traces of red and green lacquer paint
rank of figures in a long trench

evidence.title: Qin State- Terracotta Kneeling Archer, Painted

lineage.root: The earliest figurative style in the ceramics data. It follows Chinese tomb custom, which put clay attendants in the grave in place of living people.

emotion.target_response: Awe at a silent army: the viewer sees one man, then thousands, and feels the weight of an emperor's will and of a single workshop.

use_cases: a museum label or exhibition text
a prompt for a life-size clay soldier
a game asset in unglazed grey terracotta
a sculpture brief for a rank of figures
avoid_when: the brief wants a glazed Tang tomb figure with three colours
the brief needs a small decorative figurine
the brief wants a smooth porcelain surface

modifiers.how: Change to a white earthenware body, add lead glazes in amber, green and cream, and cut the scale to 30 to 80 cm.
Change to a white porcelain biscuit body, cut the height to 20 to 40 cm and keep the surface matt.

wall_thickness.note: The torso wall is 2 to 4 cm; the legs are solid.
